decisions.decision: How should document classifications be computed and delivered?
decisions.context: Millions of documents arrive each day, with volume varying substantially by season. The brief gives no per-document latency target, so scheduled scoring can meet the stated scale without assuming real-time delivery.

alternatives.label: Scheduled batch prediction deployment
pros: Daily volume: scores large workloads in batches
Seasonal demand: schedule work around demand
cons: Freshness: results wait for the next run

alternatives.label: Queue-fronted online serving cluster
pros: Daily volume: distributes scoring across predictors
cons: Cost: capacity must support online demand
Unspecified latency: adds needless serving complexity

decisions.rationale: Daily volume and absent latency requirements favor scheduled batch scoring, as described in “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “Three Levels of ML Software.” This gives up immediate per-document results; the point check returned no warnings, though its combination was unattested.
consequences: Classification results are available after each scoring run.
Run frequency must balance freshness and compute cost.

decisions.decision: How should production quality drift be detected?
decisions.context: Operators need visibility when classification quality drifts. The design space’s monitoring dimension has low exclusivity, so monitoring practices can be combined; this ADR chooses drift monitoring as the primary practice.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
pros: Quality drift: surfaces input and distribution changes
Daily volume: monitors data without manual review of every item
cons: Quality drift: drift is an indirect signal of prediction quality

alternatives.label: Passive production operation
cons: Quality drift: provides no active visibility

alternatives.label: Periodic model health checks
cons: Quality drift: issues may go unseen between checks

decisions.rationale: Quality drift visibility decides the choice: “MLOps Principles” and “Machine Learning Monitoring: What It Is, and What We Are Missing” support watching input changes, while the checked point had no warnings but was unattested. Add prediction-quality measurement when labels become available; the design space treats monitoring as combinable, but the point tool warns when multiple monitoring values are checked together.
consequences: Drift alerts require investigation and do not alone prove quality loss.
Label availability and delay determine when prediction quality can be measured.

decisions.decision: How should compute capacity respond to seasonal workload?
decisions.context: Demand swings seasonally, so the system must handle peaks without keeping peak capacity idle year-round. No hard cost or latency target is stated.

alternatives.label: Elastic resource scaling
pros: Seasonal demand: scales compute with workload
Daily volume: supports larger processing peaks
cons: Compute cost: scaling policy needs tuning

alternatives.label: Scale-to-zero serving
pros: Compute cost: removes idle serving capacity
cons: Daily volume: cold starts may delay resumed work

decisions.rationale: Seasonal demand and daily volume favor automatic scaling, supported by “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline.” This gives up the maximum idle-capacity savings of scale-to-zero; the checked point had no warnings but was unattested.
consequences: Capacity policies must account for seasonal peaks and batch windows.

decisions.decision: How should inference be packaged and deployed?
decisions.context: The classifier must process large and variable workloads, and the brief does not specify a particular cloud or runtime. A portable package supports scaling across managed or self-managed infrastructure.

alternatives.label: Containerized inference deployment
pros: Reproducible deployment: packages code and dependencies
Seasonal demand: deploys across managed or hybrid runtimes
cons: Compute cost: container infrastructure needs operation

alternatives.label: Model-as-dependency deployment
pros: Reproducible deployment: model ships with consuming application
cons: Seasonal demand: scaling is coupled to the application

decisions.rationale: Seasonal scaling and reproducible deployment decide the choice: “MLOps: Continuous Delivery and Automation Pipelines in Machine Learning” describes containerized inference across runtimes. This adds container operations compared with bundling the model into each application; the checked point had no warnings but was unattested.
consequences: Inference images and dependencies must be versioned and maintained.
Runtime placement remains open to managed, on-premise, or hybrid infrastructure.

uncovered: LLM provider, classifier model, and prompt/version strategy.
Ground-truth collection and label delay for measuring classification quality.
Document privacy, retention, and insurer-specific regulatory controls.
Batch cadence, freshness target, and any per-document latency service level.
